entries.note: “Mostly a nothing burger” judges the advance's significance without specifying a performance threshold.

entries.test: Public release records would establish whether GPT-5 existed as a released product on February 27, 2025.
entries.note: The later phrase “still no GPT-5” supplies a plain factual reading. “As hyped” adds a qualification absent from this assertion.
The proposition restricts “everything I have told you” to claims about scaling. The source does not identify a definite set of prior claims to assess.
The post does not identify which GPT-5 promises comprise the alleged hype, leaving no shared set of claims to test.

entries.test: Public statements by Cowen and comparable AI influencers would show whether they blamed users, while their published expectations could be compared with GPT-4.5's demonstrated results.
entries.note: This combines an observation about unmet expectations with an explicit forecast that influencers will blame users. No deadline is supplied for that forecast.

entries.test: Published evaluations or reproducible examples of GPT-4.5 hallucinating and making elementary errors would establish that those failures persisted at release.
entries.note: The claim concerns persistence of errors, not whether their frequency decreased.
“Fundamentally changed” supplies no shared standard for assessing the state of AI. The parenthetical about intended branding is also explicitly probabilistic.

entries.test: Contemporaneous benchmark results comparing GPT-4.5 with the latest Claude would show whether GPT-4.5 held only small advantages on some measures.
entries.note: “Some measures” is an existential claim, not a claim about overall superiority.

entries.test: Altman's public GPT-4.5 announcement and earlier product announcements would establish whether it omitted AGI and used unusually restrained promotional language.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph explicitly supports the added detail about not mentioning AGI.
The text does not enumerate the 2024 predictions being reaffirmed. “Underwhelming” also supplies no common performance standard.

entries.test: Investment totals, company financial disclosures, evidence of sustainable profits and durable competitive advantages, and GPT-5 release records would test the asserted industry conditions as of February 27, 2025.
entries.note: The normalization strengthens “basically no moat” to “no moat” and expands “some consulting firms” to consultancies generally. These are business and release claims with publicly assessable factual content.
Marcus endorses this imagined quotation as his own assessment. The spending comparison is independently checkable, but whether it yielded much of value is a judgment.

entries.test: Public comparisons of successive LLMs' training data, compute, and benchmark performance would show whether additional scale had produced sharply diminishing performance gains by the post's publication.
entries.note: Earlier passages explicitly say scaling was hitting a wall and that the releases vindicated that assessment. In context, this asserts an already observed slowdown.
